input.quote: 12.4 Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.
input.rationale: Section 12.4 binds only Customer, is an outright no-hire (\"hire, or employ\"), covers every Vendor employee rather than personnel involved in the Services, runs 24 months, and expressly negates any general-advertising or unsolicited-application carve-out. That fails the fallback on every material term and is walk-away territory. At the preferred position no non-solicit should bind Customer, so we flip the prohibitory operator in the same sentence so that Customer has no obligation to refrain from soliciting, hiring or employing Vendor employees, leaving the negated mechanics intact. This also aligns the operative text with Section 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no no-hire commitment.

ops.oldText: Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.
ops.newText: Customer shall have no obligation not to solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for 12 months afterward, whether the employee responds to a general advertisement or applies unsolicited.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have turned off the one-way covenant in 12.4 rather than leaving it operative: our position is no non-solicit on Customer, and this is consistent with Section 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we have made no no-hire commitment. If Vendor needs protection, we can discuss a mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months after their involvement ends, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches and no no-hire element.
proposal.summary: Neutralise the one-way no-hire in §12.4 so no non-solicit binds Customer
